items.title: Java4Shell update: attackers are now probing for the critical Java flaw
items.why: New since yesterday: scanners and early exploit attempts are hitting servers running OpenJDK 17+, and Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, Atlassian and Jenkins have posted advisories. No confirmed break-ins yet.
items.action: Update Java to the November 17 builds now, starting with internet-facing Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak and Elasticsearch, and follow vendor workarounds where no patch exists.

items.title: CISA says a Synology NAS flaw is being exploited, with ransomware hitting the devices
items.why: CISA added an unauthenticated takeover flaw in Synology DSM to its exploited list on November 18; recent attacks on Synology boxes have deployed C3RB3R ransomware. Apache Axis, REDCap and LiteLLM flaws were added too.
items.action: Update every Synology NAS to the latest DSM release, take it off the open internet, and confirm your backups are not reachable from the NAS itself.

items.title: N-able confirms hackers got into its Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud
items.why: An intruder accessed a server in N-able's hosted email filtering cloud, knocking out the admin portal, quarantine and logs in the Americas, Europe and APAC since November 16. Mail filtering still works; no data theft found so far.
items.action: Ask your MSP or N-able whether you are affected, watch for spam and phishing that quarantine would normally catch, and reset any admin passwords for the portal once it returns.

items.title: PHP releases critical security fixes for all supported versions today
items.why: PHP warned of critical flaws, including a remote code execution bug tied to session settings, with fixes due November 19 around 2 p.m. UTC. It follows October's PHP2Shell flaws, which have seen limited attacks.
items.action: Ask your web host or developer to install today's PHP update on WordPress and other PHP sites; until then, set session.upload_progress.enabled to 0 and restart PHP.

items.title: Deepfake Elon Musk livestream lured crypto users; Coinbase blocked $4.7 million
items.why: A fake YouTube 'Tesla flying car' stream with an AI Musk promised to double crypto sent to a QR code. Hundreds of Coinbase users tried to send money within two hours; Coinbase stopped about 91 percent.
items.action: Tell staff that any livestream or video promising to double money is a scam, and require a second person to approve any crypto or wire payment.

items.title: Atlassian's November update fixes 318 flaws across Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket
items.why: Atlassian's November 17 bulletin covers 52 critical and 266 high-severity entries, mostly in bundled components such as Spring and Tomcat, for its self-hosted Data Center products. Cloud customers need no action.
items.action: Upgrade self-hosted Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo and Crowd to the fixed LTS versions in Atlassian's bulletin.
